Isolating Facebook from your phone by choosing not to use the app is a good start. However, Facebook may still be able to track the websites you visit through tracking cookies in your browser (Even if you have logged out of Facebook). You may want to look into a app that essentially puts Facebook into it's own little jail in order to segregate it from everything else.

Face Slim: (https://github.com/indywidualny/FaceSlim) This is what I'm currently using. It keeps you logged into the Facebook mobile site, and can use your RSS notification stream.

Tinfoil for Facebook: (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.danvelazco.fbwrapper) This is the most popular wrapper for the Facebook mobile site. It keeps you logged into Facebook, but lacks the ability to pull notifications.

WebApps: (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tobykurien.webapps) This is a more generalized sandbox for any website you want to segregate from your normal browsing. I've used this to access Facebook, Twitter, Voat, and other sites. There's a bit of a learning curve for this one, but I think it's worth it.

As for minimizing the way Facebook tracks you: There's really not much more you can do beyond using Facebook as little as possible.
What if I use a separate browser for FB. Chrome for FB and Fire fox for everything else?

That is another way to keep Facebook segregated from your normal surfing. On my PC I use Chrome for Google and FB, and Firefox for everything else. That would work just as well on your phone. You may want to also look into installing uBlock Origin (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/ublock-origin/) on Firefox (The mobile browser supports add-ons). That will get rid of pesky ads and tracking code as well.
